title: Trusting God to Set Things Right

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the Lord your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you shall blot out the name of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget! - Deut 25:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a solemn command regarding the Amalekites, a people who had cruelly attacked the weak and shown no fear of God. Once God gave Israel rest in the land, they were to carry out God's judgment on this persistently hostile enemy. This was a specific act of divine justice against a nation whose cruelty and opposition to God's people had reached a settled, unrepentant hostility.

We should understand this as a particular judgment in redemptive history, not a general license for God's people to seek vengeance on their enemies. It belonged to a specific moment and purpose in God's dealings with Israel. Behind it lies a truth we can trust, that God does not ignore persistent, unrepentant evil forever. He is the righteous Judge who will ultimately set all things right.

For us under the new covenant, our calling is different. We are not to blot out earthly enemies, but to love them and pray for them, entrusting all judgment to God (Rom 12:19). We can leave the ultimate setting-right of every wrong in God's hands, knowing He is perfectly just and will not let evil have the final word. This frees us from the burden of revenge. One day, Christ will return as the righteous Judge and King, and every wrong will be answered. Can you release your grievances to the God who judges justly, trusting Him to set all things right in His time?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you entrust your grievances to God the righteous Judge?
2. How does trusting God's justice free you from revenge?
3. What does loving your enemies look like for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the righteous Judge who will set all things right. Free me from the burden of revenge, and help me love even my enemies. Amen.
